{{ModBox}}
'''Lingering Torment''' is a [[mod]] that increases the [[Status_Effect#Status Duration|status duration]] inflicted by Shotguns. 

==Stats==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! [[Mod#Mod Rank|Rank]]
! Effect 
! [[Mod#Attributes|Cost]]
|-
| 0 || +15% || 6
|-
| 1 || +30% || 7
|-
| 2 || +45% || 8
|-
| 3 || +60% || 9
|-
| 4 || +75% || 10
|-
| 5 || +90% || 11
|}

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*The mod's effects are only visible on Status Effects with an associated duration, either increasing the duration of the associated debuff ({{D|Puncture}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Corrosive}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Radiation}}, and {{D|Viral}}), or the number of ticks associated with DoT effects ({{D|Slash}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Gas}}, and {{D|Heat}}).
**This mod will ''not'' affect the duration of crowd control effects generated by Status Effects (staggers from {{D|Impact}} and the panic duration of  {{D|Heat}}).
**However, it ''does'' affect the duration of the freeze effect applied by  {{D|Cold}} after reaching 10 stacks.
**Increased Status Duration will slow down the Armor Strip effect of {{D|Heat}}. For example, with +100% status duration, the armor strip will occur every second instead of every half second. As a result, the full 50% armor strip will only be achieved after 4 seconds.
*Status Effects from the radial blasts of [[Syndicate]] [[Weapon Augments]] and Syndicate Weapons are not affected by this mod.

==Tips==
*This mod is ideal on shotguns with high [[status chance]], such as the {{Weapon|Boar Prime}}, {{Weapon|Hek}} and {{Weapon|Tigris}} if building for status effects.

{{ver|15.0}}

{{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Bolts from this Corpus bow deliver a one-two punch of an icy pulse, followed by a conventional explosion. Excess ammo picked up for other weapons will be converted into charges for the Lenz.

Warning, safety-protocols do not exist on this prototype.}} The '''Lenz''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} bow with several unique mechanics. It has a built-in ammo mutation to compensate for its rather small ammo pool, and it fires special bolts that inflict weak {{D|Cold}} procs within a eight meter radius before exploding and dealing a large amount of {{D|Blast}} damage within six meters. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Blast}} damage. *Arrow explodes on impacting a surface or enemy. **Direct arrow impact has a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc and stagger enemies. **Initial explosion has a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc in a '''7.2''' meter radius when impacting enemies or surfaces. **'''1.3''' seconds after the {{D|Cold}} effect, another explosion occurs in a '''7.2''' meter radius, dealing very high {{D|Blast}} damage. **Initial hit and explosions apply [[status]] separately. **Explosions require [[Line of Sight]] to deal damage. ***[[Line of Sight]] is affected by [[Punch Through]]; Sufficient amounts of Punch Through allows the explosion to deal damage to enemies not within line of sight. **{{D|Blast}} explosion does not occur if the arrow hits allies. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. *On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging anyone in their path and pinning the corpse to walls. *Innate {{M|Arrow Mutation}} effect. *Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate two {{Pol|Naramon}} polarities. {{Advantages| *Second highest base damage of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}}. *Tied with {{Weapon|Dread}} for highest [[critical chance]] of all bows. }} {{Disadvantages| *Arrows have travel time with slight arcing. *Slowest [[Fire Rate|charge speed]] of all bows. **Cannot be fired at partial charge. **If the bow is charged but not fired for more than a few seconds, the charge will be lost. *Very poor ammo economy. **Low ammo pool. **Only restores 1 unit of ammunition per ammo pickup. *[[Noise Level|Alarming]] for a bow, making it ill-suited for stealth gameplay. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 30% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Prisma Lenz}} ==Acquisition== The Lenz's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Cannot use the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod. *Having an innate arrow ammo mutation effect, the {{M|Arrow Mutation}} mod is not required with this weapon despite its tiny ammo reserve. However, as the innate mutation effect only restores one unit of ammunition per ammo pickup, the use of this mod is left to the user's discretion. *There are actually three sources of damage with the weapon. The arrow itself will deal {{D|Impact}}, then a large {{D|Cold}} proc will occur when the arrow hits an enemy or surface, before exploding with {{D|Blast}} damage. This is why if the user adds a single elemental like {{D|Electricity}}, the weapon will show both {{D|Magnetic}} and {{D|Electricity}} at the same time. *Enemies killed with the initial arrow's {{D|Impact}} damage are ragdolled and launched forward, dealing the same damage to other enemies in their path. In such cases, the explosion will not arm until the slain enemy's corpse strikes a wall, the floor, or any other piece of level geometry. The arrow will then create its detonation field at the point where the corpse 'lands'. **This function has an additional effect when using any mod that grants [[Multishot]]: should multiple arrows strike the same target simultaneously, a second detonation field will be created at the point where the enemy was originally struck. *Shooting a [[Sensor Bar]] activates the explosion. *Lenz will still have its {{D|Cold}} proc effect even if its {{D|Cold}} damage is changed into a secondary elemental damage like {{D|Viral}}. *Additional projectiles caused by [[Multishot]] or {{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} do not inflict stagger. *Additional range by {{M|Firestorm}} and {{M|Primed Firestorm}} have no effect on the explosion VFX, but do affect the explosion hitbox. ==Tips== *While the Lenz has innate ammo mutation, its small ammo pool and low ammo conversion rating means players have to make their shots count. **Using a companion with [[Fetch]] or [[Vacuum]] to automatically collect distant ammo pickups will allow the player to keep shooting as long as they can keep killing enemies (and getting ammo drops). *Shooting {{WF|Nova}}'s {{A|Antimatter Drop}} or a companion's {{M|Shelter}} with the Lenz results in its projectiles instantly skipping to the explosion phase. *{{WF|Limbo}}'s [[Rift Walk]] can protect from the explosion without having to escape the area of effect, even if already slowed by the initial proc if the player shifts planes quickly enough. *It can be helpful to aim at a nearby surface within the enemy's vicinity and use the Lenz as a timed mine layer. The innate guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc upon the arrow's impact will minimize enemy potential to escape, allowing the bulk of the {{D|Blast}} damage to reach them most of the time. *[[Shadow Stalker]] is immune to the Freeze debuff from the {{D|Cold}} proc, meaning he will be more than fast enough to escape the bubble before the {{D|Blast}} goes off. If you cannot score direct hits, it may be advisable to switch to a different weapon. ==Trivia== *The Lenz is the first bow that is not silent, and also the first bow that cannot equip {{M|Thunderbolt}}. *The Lenz's name may be a nod to [[wikipedia:Emil Lenz|Emil Lenz]], a Russian physicist who studied electromagnetism. He is most commonly known for [[wikipedia:Lenz's_law|Lenz's Law]]. *The pitch of the humming sound played when charging a shot changes with altered fire rates. A higher fire rate results in a more high pitched sound, while a slower fire rate produces a lower pitched sound. *The Corpus text on the bow translates to "AUOKZ", its meaning unknown. ==Media== File:Enrico-santi-enrico-santi-lenzbow1.jpg| File:Sean-bigham-072.jpg File:Sean-bigham-072prog02.jpg|Concept art File:Sean-bigham-072prog01.jpg File:Lenz 1.png|Lenz in the Arsenal File:Lenz 3.png Lenz 02.png| The "quiver" Lenz uses Lenz Default Arrow.jpg|Lenz arrow with default colours. {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|rVSYOIpPS6A|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|aMtiArSEMG4|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|cqaoSgji4DQ|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|4fsL7OqL9Gk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|5w6RKcSGZrI|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|uuSoGrvlpbM|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 1 Ammo per Pick Up: *Lenz ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|28.3}} *Cleaned up the Lenz FX. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Lenz: 70% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|25.7}} *While reviewing Bow stats the team has also refreshed all their FX (including the Lenz)! {{ver|25.5}} *Adjusted the default holster position of the Lenz Quiver so it sits closer to Warframe's backs. {{ver|25.2}} *Fixed the Bow Dryad Skin having misaligned strings when equipped on the Lenz. {{ver|25.0.8}} *Fixed the Lenz jets still appearing when you apply the Dryad Bow Skin. {{ver|22.6}} *Fixed arrow skins not showing when equipped with the Lenz. {{ver|21.7.1}} *Fixed shooting Frost’s Snow Globe from the outside with the Lenz resulting in the Blast damage applying twice instead of Cold then Blast. {{ver|21.5}} *Fixed Mirage’s Hall of Mirrors not making the strap on Lenz's quiver go invisible. {{ver|21.3}} *Introduced. }} {{ver/Lu|23.0.3}} {{ResearchNav}} {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Lenz]] [[es:Lenz]] [[ru:Ленц]] [[Category:Corpus Weapons]] [[Category:Impact Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Corpus]] [[Category:Research]] [[Category:Single-Shot]] [[Category:Update 21]] [[Category:Weapons with Passives]] [[Category:Slow]] [[uk:Ленц]]

{{ResourceInfobox}}''' Lex Incarnon Genesis''' is an item that is used to add [[Incarnon]] upgrades to the {{Weapon|Lex}} or {{Weapon|Lex Prime}}.

==Acquisition==
*Upon completion of [[The Duviri Paradox]] and [[Angels of the Zariman]], and unlocking [[The Steel Path]], players can earn '''Lex Incarnon Genesis''' from [[The Circuit]]'s Steel Path to place on their Lex with the help of [[Cavalero]] in the [[Chrysalith]]. This [[Incarnon Genesis]] form grants it evolutions to a transformation and newfound strength.
*Purchased from Cavalero for {{pc|120}}, complete with the resources used in its installation. This purchase can only be made '''once'''.

==Incarnon Genesis==

*Installing the Lex Incarnon Genesis requires 20 {{Resource|Pathos Clamp|Pathos Clamps}}, 70 {{Resource|Yao Shrub|Yao Shrubs}}, and 150 {{Resource|Saggen Pearl|Saggen Pearls}}.
**When installed, the first Evolution tier is unlocked. Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 [[affinity]] to the weapon, affected by [[Affinity Booster]]s.

===Overview===
*Incarnon Form is charged by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by achieving [[Enemy Body Parts|weakpoint hits]] and then pressing the [[Alternate Fire]] button. '''10''' weakpoints hits will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
** Charges '''do''' generate when hitting weak points highlighted by {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}}. 
*** However, they do not generate from hits on {{A|Crystallize}}'s crystalline growths.
**Weakpoints on corpses or [[Invulnerable]] targets do '''not''' build charges.
**Individual [[Multishot]] bullets can build charges.
*Mode switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's [[reload speed]].
*Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
*Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Lex's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing '''2''' rounds to a maximum of '''20'''. Once all ammunition is expended, the Lex reverts to its normal form.
**Incarnon Form's magazine is '''not''' affected by mods.
**Incarnon Form is '''not''' affected by [[Ammo Efficiency]] (such as {{A|Energized Munitions}}).
**Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, [[bleedout]], or being [[disarm]]ed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon [[death]].

<section begin=intro />
'''Lizzie''' is {{WF|Temple}}'s [[Exalted Weapon|Exalted]] Flamethrower, summoned by activating the ability {{A|Exalted Solo}}. Her primary fire shoots streams of {{D|Heat}}, while [[Zoom|aiming]] down sights and casting abilities fire {{D|Viral}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Cold}}, or {{D|Corrosive}} projectiles.<section end=intro />

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals pure {{D|Heat}} damage.
*Primary fire shoots a continuous stream of {{D|Heat}}.
**The zone of impact or maximum beam range has a spherical blast radius of '''4''' meters, allowing it to hit multiple enemies at once.
***Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}).
***Area of effect does not inflict [[Stagger|self-stagger]] and has no [[Damage Falloff]].
***[[Multishot]] has no effect on the radial damage like other AoE [[Continuous Weapon]]s.
*While [[Zoom|aiming]], casting abilities fires a {{D|Viral}} ({{Keybind|1}}), {{D|Magnetic}} ({{Keybind|2}}), {{D|Cold}} ({{Keybind|3}}), or {{D|Corrosive}} ({{Keybind|4}}) sonic projectile, with a guaranteed status effect of their respective element and {{D|Impact}}.
**Cost '''2''' ammo to fire.
**All sonic projectiles have innate '''1.4''' meter [[punch through]].
**Time the [[Temple/Abilities#Passive|Backbeat]] to apply '''3''' guaranteed status effects.

'''Advantages:'''
*Pinpoint [[accuracy]].
**{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on her.

'''Disadvantages:'''
*Requires timed [[Temple/Abilities#Passive|Backbeat]] ability casts to charge '''55''' ammo. Exalted Solo cannot be used when the fuel gauge is empty.
*Limited range of 10 meters.
**Can be increased with {{M|Sinister Reach}}.

==Notes==
*Lizzie uses [[Rifle Mods]].
*Lizzie appears in the [[Arsenal]] after unlocking Temple's {{A|Exalted Solo}} ability.

==Trivia==
*Sonic projectiles fired by Lizzie contain words written in [[1999 Language|1999 script]], which translate to "wither", "crush", "chill", and "melt", for {{D|Viral}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Cold}}, and {{D|Corrosive}} projectiles, respectively.
